Classes and interfaces.

=== fields, a constructor and methods
-- script/main --
class Counter {
  count = 0
  step: number
  constructor(step: number) {
    this.step = step
  }
  add(): Counter {
    this.count += this.step
    return this
  }
}
export function main(): number {
  const c = new Counter(3)
  c.add().add()
  return c.count
}
-- want --
6

=== field values run before the constructor's body
-- script/main --
class A {
  x = 1
  y: number
  constructor() { this.y = this.x + 1 }
}
export function main(): number { return new A().y }
-- want --
2

=== inheritance, super and overrides
-- script/main --
class Animal {
  name: string
  constructor(name: string) { this.name = name }
  sound(): string { return "..." }
  describe(): string { return this.name + " says " + this.sound() }
}
class Dog extends Animal {
  tricks = 0
  constructor(name: string) {
    super(name + " the dog")
    this.tricks = 2
  }
  sound(): string { return "woof" }
  describe(): string { return super.describe() + " and knows " + str(this.tricks) + " tricks" }
}
export function main(): string {
  const a: Animal = new Dog("Rex")
  return a.describe()
}
-- want --
"Rex the dog says woof and knows 2 tricks"

=== a subclass without a constructor takes its base's
-- script/main --
class Base {
  v: number
  constructor(v: number) { this.v = v }
}
class Derived extends Base {
  w = 5
}
export function main(): number {
  const d = new Derived(2)
  return d.v + d.w
}
-- want --
7

=== a derived constructor calls super first
-- script/main --
class Base {}
class Derived extends Base {
  constructor() { let x = 1 }
}
export function main(): number { return 1 }
-- compile error --
the constructor of Derived must call super(…) first

=== an override keeps the signature
-- script/main --
class Base { f(a: number): number { return a } }
class Derived extends Base { f(a: string): number { return 1 } }
export function main(): number { return 1 }
-- compile error --
f overrides Base.f(a: number): number with another signature

=== private members
-- script/main --
class Safe {
  private secret = 42
  private hint(): string { return "x" }
  peek(): number { return this.secret }
}
export function main(): number { return new Safe().secret }
-- compile error --
script/main:6:52: secret is private to Safe

=== private members inside the class
-- script/main --
class Safe {
  private secret = 42
  peek(other: Safe): number { return other.secret + this.secret }
}
export function main(): number { const s = new Safe(); return s.peek(s) }
-- want --
84

=== readonly fields are set only by the constructor
-- script/main --
class P {
  readonly x: number
  constructor() { this.x = 1 }
  move(): void { this.x = 2 }
}
export function main(): number { return new P().x }
-- compile error --
script/main:4:23: x is readonly

=== a field without a type needs a literal
-- script/main --
class P {
  x = 1 + 1
}
export function main(): number { return 1 }
-- compile error --
the field x needs a type

=== classes are nominal
-- script/main --
class A { x = 1 }
class B { x = 1 }
export function main(): number {
  let a: A = new B()
  return a.x
}
-- compile error --
a is a B, not a A

=== interfaces are structural
-- script/main --
interface HasX { readonly x: number; total(): number }
class A { x = 1; total(): number { return this.x } }
class B { x = 2; y = 3; total(): number { return this.x + this.y } }
function sum(items: HasX[]): number {
  let s = 0
  for (const i of items) { s += i.x + i.total() }
  return s
}
export function main(): number { return sum([new A(), new B()]) }
-- want --
9

=== implements is checked at the class
-- script/main --
interface Named { name(): string }
class Thing implements Named {
  name(): number { return 1 }
}
export function main(): number { return 1 }
-- compile error --
script/main:2:7: Thing doesn't implement Named: name is (): number, not (): string

=== an interface extends interfaces
-- script/main --
interface A { a(): number }
interface B extends A { b(): number }
class C implements B {
  a(): number { return 1 }
  b(): number { return 2 }
}
export function main(): number {
  const x: B = new C()
  const y: A = x
  return x.b() + y.a()
}
-- want --
3

=== optional methods may be left out, and scripts don't call them
-- script/main --
import { Greeter } from "test"
class Plain implements Greeter {
  greet(name: string): string { return "hi " + name }
}
export function main(): string {
  const g: Greeter = new Plain()
  return g.hello()
}
-- compile error --
hello is optional, so only the host calls it

=== a class may give an optional method
-- script/main --
import { Greeter } from "test"
class Polite implements Greeter {
  greet(name: string): string { return "good day, " + name }
  hello(): string { return "hello" }
}
export function main(): string {
  const g: Greeter = new Polite()
  return g.greet("you")
}
-- want --
"good day, you"

=== an optional method keeps its signature
-- script/main --
import { Greeter } from "test"
class Odd implements Greeter {
  greet(name: string): string { return name }
  hello(): number { return 1 }
}
export function main(): number { return 1 }
-- compile error --
Odd doesn't implement Greeter: hello is (): number, not (): string

=== type aliases
-- script/main --
type Name = string
type Names = Name[]
export function main(): Names {
  let n: Names = ["a"]
  n.push("b")
  return n
}
-- want --
["a", "b"]

=== a class extending itself
-- script/main --
class A extends B {}
class B extends A {}
export function main(): number { return 1 }
-- compile error --
extends itself

=== objects compare by identity
-- script/main --
class A {}
export function main(): bool {
  const a = new A()
  const b = a
  return a == b && a != new A()
}
-- want --
true

=== methods of null fail
-- script/main --
class A { f(): number { return 1 } }
export function main(): number {
  let a: A
  return a.f()
}
-- eval error --
script/main:4:12: f() of null

=== host classes are the host's
-- script/main --
import { probe, Probe } from "test"
export function main(): string {
  const p: Probe = probe("p1")
  return p.name + ":" + str(p.twice(21))
}
-- want --
"p1:42"

=== host errors fail the call where it was made
-- script/main --
import { probe } from "test"
export function main(): number { return probe("p").twice(-1) }
-- eval error --
script/main:2:52: twice: no negative numbers

=== host classes can't be made or extended
-- script/main --
import { Probe } from "test"
class Mine extends Probe {}
export function main(): number { return 1 }
-- compile error --
Probe is the host's, and can't be extended

=== host fields are readonly
-- script/main --
import { probe } from "test"
export function main(): number {
  const p = probe("p")
  p.name = "q"
  return 1
}
-- compile error --
name is readonly
